data.title: Pentamidine
data.summary: Other antiparasitics · Aromatic diamidine; antiprotozoal and anti-Pneumocystis
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antiparasitics_

**Class:** Aromatic diamidine; antiprotozoal and anti-Pneumocystis

## Mechanism of action
- Interferes with parasite DNA, RNA, phospholipid and protein synthesis (binds kinetoplast DNA)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Cutaneous leishmaniasis due to L. guyanensis (New World) — drug of choice
- Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (treatment and aerosolised prophylaxis when co-trimoxazole cannot be used)
- Early-stage African trypanosomiasis (T. b. gambiense); visceral leishmaniasis (second-line, historical)

## Dose & formulations
- Leishmaniasis: 4 mg/kg IM/IV on alternate days for 3–4 doses (L. guyanensis) or longer courses
- PCP: 4 mg/kg IV daily for 21 days; prophylaxis 300 mg nebulised monthly

## Adverse effects
- Hypoglycaemia (pancreatic β-cell toxicity — early), followed later by diabetes mellitus
- Hypotension (especially with rapid IV infusion — give slowly lying down), arrhythmias (QT prolongation)
- Nephrotoxicity, pancreatitis, leucopenia; sterile abscess at IM sites

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity; caution in diabetes, heart disease, renal impairment

## Drug interactions
- Foscarnet (severe hypocalcaemia), nephrotoxic and QT drugs

## Monitoring
- Blood glucose, BP during and after infusion, ECG, renal function, CBC

## Pregnancy & lactation
Use only when essential.

## Viva points
- Hypoglycaemia then diabetes
- Drug of choice for L. guyanensis cutaneous leishmaniasis

_Sources: Khopkar ch.5 (Pentamidine); Wolverton 4e ch.12. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
